title: The purpose of the world: experience and liberation (2.18–2.22)
hook: the seen world exists for the seer, for two things, experience and freedom, and it doesn't vanish when one person is done

segments.voice: Yesterday: duhkha, and your line, the seen and the seer. To the discerning, all is suffering, and the cause is the two tangled together. Today ends the week.

There's an old picture in the Samkhya Karika, a related text whose map of seer and seen the Yoga Sutras share. A dancer performs on a stage. She dances and dances, until the one watching has truly seen her. Then she stops, because the dance has done its work. Patanjali has named the cause of suffering: the seer and the seen, joined. You might expect him to call the seen the enemy, the trap to escape. He does something stranger. He asks what the whole show is for, and gives it a purpose.
screen: `A DANCER ON A STAGE.` → `SHE STOPS WHEN SHE'S TRULY SEEN.` → `WHAT IS THE SHOW FOR?`

segments.voice: Sutra 2.18 describes the seen: everything that can be watched, the mountains, the body, the senses, the mind itself. Its nature is light, activity and stillness, the three qualities of nature. And its purpose is two things: experience and liberation. Bhoga and apavarga. The world is there so the seer can taste it, and so the seer can finally be free of the confusion. Both, not one instead of the other. Then 2.20 describes the seer: pure seeing, nothing more. Though pure, it looks out through the ideas of the mind, and so it seems to take their color. And 2.21 is the short, bold line: the seen exists only for the seer's sake. Then 2.22 adds something tender. When one person's purpose is done, the world doesn't disappear. It stays, because it is shared with everyone else still dancing and watching. Nobody's freedom switches the lights off for the rest. Now the week, from the top. Ignorance: mistaking the passing for the permanent. I-ness: mistaking the instrument for the one who sees. Attraction and aversion, the pull and the push. Fear of death, even in the wise. Karma, the storehouse, where it all ripens. To the discerning, all is suffering. And today, the turn: the same world that tangles is there for freedom. Seven days of diagnosis, and the last one ends with a reason.
screen: `BHOGA AND APAVARGA.` · `THE SEER: PURE SEEING.` · `THE SEEN EXISTS FOR THE SEER.` · `IT STAYS FOR EVERYONE ELSE.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `FOR THE SEER.`

segments.voice: First, experience: let one sense fill up, the sounds in the room or the light through your eyelids, and taste it fully without grabbing. Then freedom: notice that the sound comes and goes, and the hearing stays. Move between the two, tasting and watching, as many times as you like.
Apavarga, release, liberation. In the Yoga Sutras, the seen exists for the seer, for two things: experience and liberation.
Your line: for the seer. Experience and liberation, both. That's the week, day four hundred fifty-five.

screen: `DAY 455 COUNTS.` → `A WEEK OF THE AFFLICTIONS, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: DISCERNMENT IS THE WAY.`

howItsDone: In the Samkhya and Yoga schools, the world of nature is understood to exist for the sake of awareness, offering both experience and the chance of liberation; students study these sutras with the classical commentary and reflect on them in meditation.

fork.setup: one seer finally sees clearly. its purpose is done. what happens to the world?
options: it no longer binds that seer, but stays for everyone else.
nothing changes, so the work was pointless.
fork.reveal: 2.22: though it has ceased for the one whose purpose is done, it hasn't ceased, because it is common to others.

original.note: Sanskrit apavarga: release, liberation; paired in 2.18 with bhoga, experience.

trapdoor: what you thought: spiritual people want to escape the world.
what it means: in the Yoga Sutras the world has a job: to give the seer experience, and then freedom.

what a scholar hears: 2.18 links the three gunas (light, activity, stillness) to bhoga and apavarga; 2.21 says the seen exists for the seer; 2.22 keeps the world real for others, a point against reading yoga as world-denial.
recall: the mind takes the object's form

chat.says: If the seer is meant to be free, isn't the world just a trap to escape?
options: No. Patanjali says the seen is for the seer: for experience and for liberation.
Yes. The seen exists only to trap the seer, so it has no purpose at all.
No. Once a single person is free, the world vanishes for everyone else too.
chat.meaning: Sutra 2.18 gives the seen two purposes, bhoga and apavarga, experience and liberation, and 2.21 says it exists for the seer's sake.
